Shakespeare

The First Chapter, called
BEING A TRUE ACCOUNT OF A CITY OUTSIDE TIME

Thou wak’st where borrow’d verses lie asleep,
In rooms a dead man’s secrets still would keep.
The city sings, the bridge begins to sway;
Below, the plague; above, a night of prey.
Through fog and cradles, stars and iron rail,
One door is left before thy lamp shall fail —
Wilt thou escape the London of his play?
Imprinted at London, in the Yeare of Our Lord 1606

“A plague o’ both your houses!” so he cried,
Young Mercutio, who for their quarrel died.
Mark thou the houses twain that bred such hate:
The Rose of Capulet, the Ivy gate
Of Montague. The Crown and Bell spare thou,
For they had naught to do with that old vow.
When both are cross’d in red, as plague-men do,
The gate shall rise and let the living through.

This week the bells have toll’d for many more;
Red crosses bloom on every stricken door.
The rats grow fat, the doctors walk in beaks,

When gaslight gutters, then he walks abroad;
When lamps burn full, he stands as still as stone.
From this same Post he sets upon his road,
And stops six times, and every time alone.

For I’ll not send a guess to Scotland Yard.
Then on my plan, in order, trace his walk,
And I shall lift the bar from Mourning Gate.
He comes again, if once thou lose his trail —
But who would walk his road, and not grow pale?

When first we built this bridge, it would not stand;
The river tore each stone out of our hand.
Then spake the master: “Give the flood its due.”
We took a maid, a child of years but few,
And walled her in the pier, and sang the while
That London Bridge should stand a thousand mile.
“Set a man to watch,” we sang, “all night.”
Her key we cast away beyond all sight.
My fair lady sleeps beneath the arch;
The witches sing to wake her, and she’ll march.
Whoever treads her bridge when she doth wake
Shall fall with London Bridge, for her sake.

What the walls remember

Above each little bed a bell doth hang,
And in each woven hoop a charm is strung:
A lamp, a crescent moon, a cradle, and a door.

A faulty note unsings what thou hast done;
The box will play again for anyone.
But hush — the chair still rocks, the dolls still stare —
Who sits so still, and never leaves her chair?
